answer.rationale: Competitor price cut is acute threat to SMB churn; memory_73 confirms targeted promotional pricing is effective acquisition and revenue lift for price-sensitive SMB segments. memory_31 shows signup simplification also works on SMB but addresses activation, not retention under price pressure. Referral incentives (memory_57) add qualified revenue but don't directly defend against churn. Activation messaging (memory_91) improves engagement but won't retain price-competitive accounts. Enterprise sales assist doesn't address SMB base at risk. Promotional pricing is most direct defense, but with caution: pricing moves create path dependency and margin pressure. Small guarded test allows us to measure churn arrest and revenue impact before broad commitment. Preserves optionality to combine with activation messaging or simplification if needed. High confidence in tactical fit; moderate confidence in long-term margin sustainability.
